title: Q3 Rapid Canaries: Dedicated Pool Slice Experiments & Autoscale Backstop Strategy
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Objective: Design and run a set of ‘rapid canary’ experiments that validate autoscale fallback and fast-fail behaviors for Dedicated GPU pools under realistic surge patterns. This work creates a concise playbook (runbook + dashboards + rollback fences) operators and SREs can use during launch windows and incidents.

Why this differs: instead of a single monolithic autoscale rollout, we will slice capacity into small, observable canaries that stress specific failure modes (queue saturation, prewarm miss, cross-region latency). Each canary is deliberately configured to fail fast so we can validate detection, automated backstops, and manual escalation paths without risking broad customer impact.

Scope: launching 3 parallel canary slices per region (us-east-1, eu-west-1), instrumenting trace-level telemetry, dashboard panels, and an automated backstop policy that triggers: 1) immediate priority fallback to warm reservoir; 2) model-variant downgrade policy; 3) routing to hosted tiers for affected routes. Deliverables include the playbook doc, dashboard templates, a GitHub PR with telemetry hooks, and a simulated load test harness.

Out of scope: long-term autoscale policy tuning, billing model changes, and Dedicated offering UX changes (console deep integrations will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Three canary slices deployed to staging and can be toggled via feature flag. 2) Dashboards show key signals (queue depth, tail latency p95/p99, prewarm hit rate, backstop activations). 3) Automated backstop policy successfully routes 95% of test traffic away from failing slice and keeps tail latency under target for dependent routes during tests. 4) Playbook contains clear abort/rollback steps and contact list. 5) Post-mortem template and decision log created after each canary run.
success_metrics:
- Canaries expose at least two previously-untested failure modes within first two runs.
- Automated backstop triggers within 30s of defined threshold in >=90% of simulated failures.
- Runbook execution time (identify->route->notify) under 5 minutes in >80% of runs.
- No customer-facing errors in production during controlled rollouts.
